column1: # Golden review-grid flags: real model output that must not pass silently.
# source <TAB> malayalam_output <TAB> expected <TAB> back_translation / note
# expected is one of:
#   problem  — demonstrably wrong; the operator must fix it
#   check    — nothing can vouch for it; the operator must read it
#   clean    — must raise nothing at all
#   library  — never reaches the model: the word library answers it outright
#   composed — built from trade terms alone; never reaches the model
#   gap      — known and accepted: nothing here catches this one. See below.
# MEASURED. Every row is real output from opus-mt-en-ml over a realistic
# 18-string price list, recorded in NEXT.md 1.6 on 2026-08-26. At the time, the
# ONLY detector that fired was a word-count heuristic, on 4 rows — every row
# below came back `needs_attention: false`.
# Why these are the hard cases: a word-count heuristic cannot fire on a
# one-word cell, and one-word cells are exactly the product names. The `clean`
# rows exist to stop the fix from flagging everything, which would be the same
# failure wearing the opposite coat.
# ADR-032 changed what the right answer is for most of them. A warning saying
# "nothing here can check this, go and add a glossary entry" was the best this
# file could ask for while the tool did not know the word. It knows now, so the
# assertion is no longer "was it flagged?" but the far stronger "did it come
# back correct, without the model being consulted at all?".
# The `gap` row is the honest cost of that change, and it is written down rather
# than quietly dropped: `Focus Digitals` is a proper noun, no dictionary will
# ever hold it, and the short-cell warning that used to catch it is gone. It is
# covered instead by the corrections memory the first time the operator fixes
# it (ADR-029) — but until they do, nothing here fires.
